claim: Adamts6 mRNA is reduced in limb and lung of Adamts6-mutant mice compared to wild type levels.
source: qRT-PCR analysis showed that Adamts6 mRNA was reduced in limb and lung with respect to wild type levels in Adamts6-mutant mice [which have a missense Ser149Arg mutation that abrogates protein secretion, essentially comprising a knockout (Prins et al., 2018)]
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data presented in the manuscript and references a prior publication (Prins et al., 2018) for characterization of the mutation.

claim: Adamts6 mRNA is consistently increased in Adamts10-/- tissues.
source: qRT-PCR analysis showed that Adamts6 mRNA was reduced in limb and lung with respect to wild type levels in Adamts6-mutant mice [which have a missense Ser149Arg mutation that abrogates protein secretion, essentially comprising a knockout (Prins et al., 2018)], but was consistently increased in Adamts10-/- tissues (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Adamts10 mRNA is undetectable in Adamts10-/- mice.
source: Adamts10 mRNA was undetectable in Adamts10-/- mice (which have an intragenic IRES-lacZ insertion that disrupts mRNA continuity)
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data and describes the nature of the knockout allele.

claim: Adamts10 mRNA is increased in Adamts6-/- tissues.
source: Adamts10 mRNA was undetectable in Adamts10-/- mice (which have an intragenic IRES-lacZ insertion that disrupts mRNA continuity), and increased in Adamts6-/- tissues (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Each gene (Adamts6 and Adamts10) shows reciprocal increased expression when either is inactivated, suggestive of transcriptional adaptation.
source: Thus, each gene shows reciprocal increased expression when either is inactivated, suggestive of transcriptional adaptation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the qRT-PCR data showing reciprocal upregulation of Adamts6 in Adamts10-/- mice and vice versa.

claim: mRNA for Adamts17 and Adamts19 were unchanged in Adamts6- or Adamts10-deficient tissues.
source: In contrast, mRNA for Adamts17, also linked to WMS (Morales et al., 2009), and its homolog Adamts19 were unchanged in Adamts6- or Adamts10-deficient tissues (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A and cites a prior publication (Morales et al., 2009) linking Adamts17 to WMS.

claim: Neither ADAMTS10 nor furin-optimized ADAMTS10 cleaved ADAMTS6.
source: Neither ADAMTS10 nor furin-optimized ADAMTS10 cleaved ADAMTS6 and ADAMTS6 did not cleave ADAMTS10 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ADAMTS6 did not cleave ADAMTS10.
source: Neither ADAMTS10 nor furin-optimized ADAMTS10 cleaved ADAMTS6 and ADAMTS6 did not cleave ADAMTS10 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adamts6-/- embryos have severe reduction of crown to rump length at E14.5, E16.5 and E18.5.
source: Adamts6-/- embryos had severe reduction of crown to rump length, measured at E14.5, E16.5 and E18.5, which was also statistically significant in Adamts10-/- mice at E18.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Crown to rump length reduction was statistically significant in Adamts10-/- mice at E18.5.
source: Adamts6-/- embryos had severe reduction of crown to rump length, measured at E14.5, E16.5 and E18.5, which was also statistically significant in Adamts10-/- mice at E18.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Adamts6-/- hindlimbs were severely short and internally rotated.
source: Whereas Adamts6-/- forelimbs appeared shorter, Adamts6-/- hindlimbs were severely short and internally rotated (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 4B, Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observations and measurements shown in multiple figures.

claim: Alizarin red- and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations showed reduced ossification of Adamts6-/- hindlimb distal long bones at E14.5, E16.5 and E18.5.
source: Alizarin red- and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations at embryonic day (E)14.5, when ossification is initiated, and at E16.5 and E18.5, by which time it is established, showed reduced ossification of Adamts6-/- hindlimb distal long bones and deformation of all hindlimb segments (Figure 1B, C and F)
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1B, C and F.

claim: Adamts6-/- hindlimbs showed deformation of all hindlimb segments.
source: Alizarin red- and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations at embryonic day (E)14.5, when ossification is initiated, and at E16.5 and E18.5, by which time it is established, showed reduced ossification of Adamts6-/- hindlimb distal long bones and deformation of all hindlimb segments (Figure 1B, C and F), most evident in the thicker tibia and angulated fibula (Figure 1B, C and F, arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1B, C and F.

claim: Adamts6-/- forelimbs demonstrated failure of diaphyseal remodeling and smaller ossific centers than wild type littermates after E14.5.
source: Adamts6-/- forelimbs demonstrated failure of diaphyseal remodeling (e.g. wider, tubular-appearing radius and ulna) and smaller ossific centers than wild type littermates after E14.5 (Figure 1B, C and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1B, C and E.

claim: Neither Adamts6-/- forelimbs nor hindlimbs showed skeletal patterning anomalies.
source: Neither forelimbs nor hindlimbs showed skeletal patterning anomalies.
evidence: This is an observation based on skeletal analysis of the mutant embryos.

claim: Adamts10-/- embryos had a morphologically normal appendicular skeleton without statistically significant shortening of individual long bones.
source: In contrast to Adamts6-/- embryos, Adamts10-/- embryos had a morphologically normal appendicular skeleton without statistically significant shortening of individual long bones (Figure 1—figure supplement 4; Mularczyk et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2019a).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and cites prior publications (Mularczyk et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2019a).

claim: Adamts6-/- embryos showed delayed appearance of femoral and fibular primary ossific centers.
source: Histologic comparison of alcian blue-stained hindlimb long bone sections at daily intervals from E14.5-E18.5 showed delayed appearance of femoral and fibular primary ossific centers in Adamts6-/- embyros, with persistence of hypertrophic chondrocytes and delayed vascular invasion
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis of alcian blue-stained sections.

claim: Adamts6-/- embryos showed persistence of hypertrophic chondrocytes and delayed vascular invasion in femur and fibula.
source: Histologic comparison of alcian blue-stained hindlimb long bone sections at daily intervals from E14.5-E18.5 showed delayed appearance of femoral and fibular primary ossific centers in Adamts6-/- embyros, with persistence of hypertrophic chondrocytes and delayed vascular invasion
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis of alcian blue-stained sections.

claim: In Adamts6-/- tibia, the primary ossific center appeared on schedule, but was persistently smaller.
source: in the tibia, the primary ossific center appeared on schedule, but was persistently smaller (Figure 1—figure supplements 6–8).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 6–8.

claim: The distal tibia and fibula showed pronounced angulation as early as E14.5, persisting through E18.5 in Adamts6-/- embryos.
source: The distal tibia and fibula showed pronounced angulation as early as E14.5, persisting through E18.5 (Figure 1—figure supplements 7–8).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 7–8.

claim: Mineral deposition at E14.5 was reduced in the perichondrium/periosteum and within the primary center hypertrophic zones in Adamts6-/- femur and tibia.
source: Mineral deposition, visualized by von Kossa staining at E14.5, was reduced in the perichondrium/periosteum as well as within the primary center hypertrophic zones in Adamts6-/- femur and tibia and undetectable in the fibula as compared to control (Figure 1—figure supplement 9A, B)
evidence: The claim is supported by von Kossa staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 9A, B.

claim: Mineral deposition at E14.5 was undetectable in Adamts6-/- fibula.
source: Mineral deposition, visualized by von Kossa staining at E14.5, was reduced in the perichondrium/periosteum as well as within the primary center hypertrophic zones in Adamts6-/- femur and tibia and undetectable in the fibula as compared to control (Figure 1—figure supplement 9A, B)
evidence: The claim is supported by von Kossa staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 9A, B.

claim: By E18.5, mineralization was seen in each primary center of Adamts6-/- hindlimb bones.
source: whereas by E18.5, mineralization was seen in each primary center (Figure 1—figure supplement 9C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by von Kossa staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 9C, D.

claim: E18.5 Adamts6-/- embryos had shortened, tubular ribs.
source: The axial and craniofacial skeleton were also abnormal in E18.5 Adamts6-/- embryos, with shortened, tubular ribs, absence of sternal segmentation and under-ossified xiphoid processes (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: E18.5 Adamts6-/- embryos had absence of sternal segmentation.
source: The axial and craniofacial skeleton were also abnormal in E18.5 Adamts6-/- embryos, with shortened, tubular ribs, absence of sternal segmentation and under-ossified xiphoid processes (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: E18.5 Adamts6-/- embryos had under-ossified xiphoid processes.
source: The axial and craniofacial skeleton were also abnormal in E18.5 Adamts6-/- embryos, with shortened, tubular ribs, absence of sternal segmentation and under-ossified xiphoid processes (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Adamts6-/- vertebral bodies were smaller in size with corresponding size reduction of all vertebral ossification centers.
source: Additionally, their vertebral bodies were smaller in size with corresponding size reduction of all vertebral ossification centers.
evidence: This is an observation based on skeletal analysis of E18.5 Adamts6-/- embryos.

claim: Adamts6-/- craniofacial skeletons had reduced anterior-posterior and nasal-occipital dimensions.
source: Adamts6-/- craniofacial skeletons had reduced anterior-posterior and nasal-occipital dimensions, a corresponding reduction in size of individual elements, delayed ossification of parietal bones and wider anterior fontanelles (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Adamts6-/- craniofacial skeletons had delayed ossification of parietal bones.
source: Adamts6-/- craniofacial skeletons had reduced anterior-posterior and nasal-occipital dimensions, a corresponding reduction in size of individual elements, delayed ossification of parietal bones and wider anterior fontanelles (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Adamts6-/- craniofacial skeletons had wider anterior fontanelles.
source: Adamts6-/- craniofacial skeletons had reduced anterior-posterior and nasal-occipital dimensions, a corresponding reduction in size of individual elements, delayed ossification of parietal bones and wider anterior fontanelles (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos demonstrated markedly more severe external anomalies than Adamts6-/- mutants including subcutaneous hemorrhage, micrognathia and an omphalocele.
source: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos demonstrated markedly more severe external anomalies than Adamts6-/- mutants including subcutaneous hemorrhage, micrognathia and an omphalocele, along with more severe forelimb and hindlimb dysmorphology (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had more severe forelimb and hindlimb dysmorphology than Adamts6-/- mutants.
source: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos demonstrated markedly more severe external anomalies than Adamts6-/- mutants including subcutaneous hemorrhage, micrognathia and an omphalocele, along with more severe forelimb and hindlimb dysmorphology (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had the greatest reduction of nose-rump length among all genotypes.
source: Skeletal preparations showed more severe hindlimb anomalies than in Adamts6-/- mutants and appearance of forelimb abnormalities similar in degree of severity to Adamts6-/- hindlimbs with externally evident shortening, the greatest reduction of nose-rump length among all genotypes and the shortest long bones among the generated genotypes (Figure 1D–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric data shown in Figure 1D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had the shortest long bones among the generated genotypes.
source: Skeletal preparations showed more severe hindlimb anomalies than in Adamts6-/- mutants and appearance of forelimb abnormalities similar in degree of severity to Adamts6-/- hindlimbs with externally evident shortening, the greatest reduction of nose-rump length among all genotypes and the shortest long bones among the generated genotypes (Figure 1D–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric data shown in Figure 1D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Fibular ossification was minimal in Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos.
source: Fibular ossification was minimal, and the zeugopods showed pronounced tibio-fibular angulation (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The zeugopods showed pronounced tibio-fibular angulation in Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos.
source: Fibular ossification was minimal, and the zeugopods showed pronounced tibio-fibular angulation (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had shortened and tubular ribs.
source: The shortened and tubular ribs, vertebral bodies with smaller ossification centers, lack of xiphoid process ossification and poor ossification of cranial bones resulting in larger fontanelles, further demonstrated more severe impairment of axial and craniofacial skeletal development than in Adamts6-/- embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had vertebral bodies with smaller ossification centers.
source: The shortened and tubular ribs, vertebral bodies with smaller ossification centers, lack of xiphoid process ossification and poor ossification of cranial bones resulting in larger fontanelles, further demonstrated more severe impairment of axial and craniofacial skeletal development than in Adamts6-/- embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had lack of xiphoid process ossification.
source: The shortened and tubular ribs, vertebral bodies with smaller ossification centers, lack of xiphoid process ossification and poor ossification of cranial bones resulting in larger fontanelles, further demonstrated more severe impairment of axial and craniofacial skeletal development than in Adamts6-/- embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had poor ossification of cranial bones resulting in larger fontanelles.
source: The shortened and tubular ribs, vertebral bodies with smaller ossification centers, lack of xiphoid process ossification and poor ossification of cranial bones resulting in larger fontanelles, further demonstrated more severe impairment of axial and craniofacial skeletal development than in Adamts6-/- embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Inactivation of one Adamts6 allele in Adamts10-/- mice did not significantly worsen the observed dysmorphology and skeletal phenotype.
source: Whereas inactivation of one Adamts6 allele in Adamts10-/- mice did not significantly worsen the observed dysmorphology and skeletal phenotype, Adamts10 haploinsufficiency further reduced Adamts6-/- crown to rump length and led to shorter femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius and ulna (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Adamts10 haploinsufficiency further reduced Adamts6-/- crown to rump length.
source: Whereas inactivation of one Adamts6 allele in Adamts10-/- mice did not significantly worsen the observed dysmorphology and skeletal phenotype, Adamts10 haploinsufficiency further reduced Adamts6-/- crown to rump length and led to shorter femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius and ulna (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Adamts10 haploinsufficiency led to shorter femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius and ulna in Adamts6-/- embryos.
source: Whereas inactivation of one Adamts6 allele in Adamts10-/- mice did not significantly worsen the observed dysmorphology and skeletal phenotype, Adamts10 haploinsufficiency further reduced Adamts6-/- crown to rump length and led to shorter femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius and ulna (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Adamts6 and Adamts10 exhibited overlapping expression in E13.5 resting and proliferating zone chondrocytes and perichondrium.
source: Adamts6 and Adamts10 exhibited overlapping expression in E13.5 resting and proliferating zone chondrocytes and perichondrium (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At E14.5, both Adamts6 and Adamts10 maintained strong expression in the perichondrium.
source: At E14.5, when the first primary ossific centers are formed, both genes maintained strong expression in the perichondrium (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Adamts6 and Adamts10 are expressed in the knee joint mesenchyme.
source: They are expressed in the the knee joint mesenchyme, and Adamts6 was strongly expressed in the patellar tendon (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Adamts6 was strongly expressed in the patellar tendon.
source: They are expressed in the the knee joint mesenchyme, and Adamts6 was strongly expressed in the patellar tendon (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Both Adamts6 and Adamts10 were expressed in muscles and tendons around the hip, elbow, and ankle and in vertebral endplates.
source: Both genes were expressed in muscles and tendons around the hip, elbow, and ankle and in vertebral endplates (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: RGB trichrome-stained E18.5 sections revealed abnormal growth plate cartilage ECM in Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos, showing a dramatic reduction in staining with the alcian blue component.
source: RGB trichrome-stained E18.5 sections revealed abnormal growth plate cartilage ECM, showing a dramatic reduction in staining with the alcian blue component, which detects sulfated proteoglycans, in Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RGB trichrome staining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The perichondrium and adjacent mesenchyme showed increased and diffuse staining of collagen in the Adamts6-deficient and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femur.
source: The perichondrium and adjacent mesenchyme showed increased and diffuse staining of collagen in the Adamts6-deficient and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femur (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RGB trichrome staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The reduction of alcian blue staining and diffuse collagen staining was evident in E14.5 Adamts6-/- long bone, such as the femur.
source: The reduction of alcian blue staining and diffuse collagen staining was evident in E14.5 Adamts6-/- long bone, such as the femur (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by RGB trichrome staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- resting zone chondrocytes were tightly packed compared to wild type.
source: Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- resting zone (RZ) chondrocytes were tightly packed compared to wild type with disorganized columnar zones (CZ) and hypertrophic zones (HZ), whereas Adamts10-/- growth plates resembled the wild type (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RGB trichrome staining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- embryos had disorganized columnar zones and hypertrophic zones.
source: Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- resting zone (RZ) chondrocytes were tightly packed compared to wild type with disorganized columnar zones (CZ) and hypertrophic zones (HZ), whereas Adamts10-/- growth plates resembled the wild type (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RGB trichrome staining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Adamts10-/- growth plates resembled the wild type.
source: Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- resting zone (RZ) chondrocytes were tightly packed compared to wild type with disorganized columnar zones (CZ) and hypertrophic zones (HZ), whereas Adamts10-/- growth plates resembled the wild type (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RGB trichrome staining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Immunostaining revealed less intense aggrecan staining in Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- cartilage as compared to control and Adamts10-/- limbs.
source: To determine the basis for reduced alcian blue staining intensity, we immunostained for aggrecan, which revealed less intense staining in Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- cartilage as compared to control and Adamts10-/- limbs and in E14.5 Adamts6-/- femur (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Reduced staining of cartilage link protein was observed in E14.5 and E18.5 Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femoral growth plates.
source: Consistent with reduced aggrecan, we observed reduced staining of cartilage link protein, which stabilizes the aggregates formed by aggrecan and hyaluronan and for the key chondrogenic factor Sox9 in both E14.5 and E18.5 femoral growth plates (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Reduced staining of Sox9 was observed in E14.5 and E18.5 Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femoral growth plates.
source: Consistent with reduced aggrecan, we observed reduced staining of cartilage link protein, which stabilizes the aggregates formed by aggrecan and hyaluronan and for the key chondrogenic factor Sox9 in both E14.5 and E18.5 femoral growth plates (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Col X staining revealed comparable staining in all genotypes.
source: In contrast, the HZ marker Col X revealed comparable staining in all genotypes, and suggested increased HZ thickness in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femur as compared to wild type, potentially related to delayed ossification (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Col X staining suggested increased HZ thickness in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femur as compared to wild type.
source: In contrast, the HZ marker Col X revealed comparable staining in all genotypes, and suggested increased HZ thickness in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femur as compared to wild type, potentially related to delayed ossification (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: PCNA and TUNEL staining revealed no change in cell proliferation or cell death, respectively, in Adamts6-/- femoral cartilage.
source: PCNA and TUNEL staining revealed no change in cell proliferation or cell death, respectively, in Adamts6-/- femoral cartilage (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by PCNA and TUNEL staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Increased MAGP1 staining intensity was detected in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femur perichondrium.
source: First, we stained for microfibril-associated glycoprotein 1 (MAGP1), which binds to both fibrillin-1 and fibrillin-2 (Jensen et al., 2001), to report their combined abundance and detected increased staining intensity in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- femur perichondrium (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, and cites a prior publication (Jensen et al., 2001) for MAGP1 binding to fibrillins.

claim: Immunostaining with a monospecific fibrillin-2 antibody showed more intense perichondrial staining in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- perichondrium.
source: Immunostaining with a monospecific fibrillin-2 antibody showed more intense perichondrial staining in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- perichondrium (Figure 4B)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Comparable fibrillin-1 staining was observed in Adamts10-/-, Adamts6-/- and Adamts6-/-;Adamts10-/- perichondrium compared to wild type.
source: but comparable fibrillin-1 staining was observed (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Fbn2 and Fbn1 mRNA levels were unchanged in Adamts6- and Adamts10-deficient hindlimbs.
source: Fbn2 and Fbn1 mRNA levels were unchanged in Adamts6- and Adamts10-deficient hindlimbs, suggesting that increased fibrillin-2 staining was not a result of increased transcription (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Increased fibrillin-2 staining was not a result of increased transcription.
source: Fbn2 and Fbn1 mRNA levels were unchanged in Adamts6- and Adamts10-deficient hindlimbs, suggesting that increased fibrillin-2 staining was not a result of increased transcription (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the qRT-PCR data showing unchanged Fbn2 mRNA levels despite increased fibrillin-2 protein staining.

claim: Co-cultures of Fbn1-/- MEFs with HEK293T cells stably expressing catalytically inactive ADAMTS6 (ADAMTS6 EA) for 6 days illustrated specific co-localization of ADAMTS6 EA with fibrillin-2 microfibrils.
source: Co-cultures of Fbn1-/- MEFs with HEK293T cells stably expressing catalytically inactive ADAMTS6 (ADAMTS6 Glu404Ala, referred to hereafter as ADAMTS6 EA) for 6 days illustrated specific co-localization of ADAMTS6 EA with fibrillin-2 microfibrils (Figure 5A, top row).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: When Fbn1-/- MEFs were co-cultured with HEK293F cells expressing active ADAMTS6, no fibrillin-2 staining was seen.
source: When Fbn1-/- MEFs were co-cultured with HEK293F cells expressing active ADAMTS6 (Figure 5A, 2nd row), no fibrillin-2 staining was seen, suggestive of proteolytic degradation of fibrillin-2 microfibrils or interference with their assembly.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: 4-day-old cultures of Fbn2-/- mouse skin fibroblasts revealed co-localization of ADAMTS6 EA with fibrillin-1.
source: Similarly, 4-day-old cultures of Fbn2-/- mouse skin fibroblasts (MSF) revealed co-localization of ADAMTS6 EA with fibrillin-1 and demonstrated absence of fibrillin-1 microfibrils in the presence of ADAMTS6 (Figure 5A, center panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Fbn2-/- mouse skin fibroblasts demonstrated absence of fibrillin-1 microfibrils in the presence of ADAMTS6.
source: Similarly, 4-day-old cultures of Fbn2-/- mouse skin fibroblasts (MSF) revealed co-localization of ADAMTS6 EA with fibrillin-1 and demonstrated absence of fibrillin-1 microfibrils in the presence of ADAMTS6 (Figure 5A, center panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ADAMTS6 EA co-localized with fibronectin.
source: Since a fibronectin fibrillar matrix is formed soon after plating of cells and acts as a template for fibrillin microfibril assembly (Beene et al., 2013; Sabatier et al., 2009), we similarly analyzed fibronectin staining, observing that ADAMTS6 EA co-localized with fibronectin and that fibronectin fibrils were absent in the presence of ADAMTS6, suggesting also that over-expressed ADAMTS6 may cleave fibronectin (Figure 5A, bottom panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments shown in Figure 5A, and cites prior publications (Beene et al., 2013; Sabatier et al., 2009) for the role of fibronectin in microfibril assembly.

claim: Fibronectin fibrils were absent in the presence of ADAMTS6.
source: Since a fibronectin fibrillar matrix is formed soon after plating of cells and acts as a template for fibrillin microfibril assembly (Beene et al., 2013; Sabatier et al., 2009), we similarly analyzed fibronectin staining, observing that ADAMTS6 EA co-localized with fibronectin and that fibronectin fibrils were absent in the presence of ADAMTS6, suggesting also that over-expressed ADAMTS6 may cleave fibronectin (Figure 5A, bottom panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Over-expressed ADAMTS6 may cleave fibronectin.
source: Since a fibronectin fibrillar matrix is formed soon after plating of cells and acts as a template for fibrillin microfibril assembly (Beene et al., 2013; Sabatier et al., 2009), we similarly analyzed fibronectin staining, observing that ADAMTS6 EA co-localized with fibronectin and that fibronectin fibrils were absent in the presence of ADAMTS6, suggesting also that over-expressed ADAMTS6 may cleave fibronectin (Figure 5A, bottom panels).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that fibronectin fibrils were absent in the presence of active ADAMTS6.

claim: MEFs isolated from Adamts6-/- embryos showed greater fibrillin-2, fibrillin-1, and fibronectin microfibril staining intensity than wild type MEFs.
source: In agreement, MEFs isolated from Adamts6-/- embryos showed greater fibrillin-2, fibrillin-1, and fibronectin microfibril staining intensity than wild type MEFs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Biacore analysis showed that C-terminal ADAMTS6 constructs (ADAMTS6-Ct, ADAMTS6-S4TSR and ADAMTS6-4TSR) bound the C-terminal half of fibrillin-2 (fibrillin-2-Ct).
source: Biacore analysis showed that C-terminal ADAMTS6 constructs (ADAMTS6-Ct, ADAMTS6-S4TSR and ADAMTS6-4TSR) bound the C-terminal half of fibrillin-2 (fibrillin-2-Ct) (Figure 6A–C, Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by Biacore surface plasmon resonance data shown in Figure 6A–C and Table 1.

claim: The fibrillin-2 binding region of ADAMTS6 is located in the C-terminal TSR array.
source: Since all 4TSR-array-containing constructs bound to fibrillin-2-Ct we concluded that the fibrillin-2 binding region of ADAMTS6 was located in the C-terminal TSR array.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Biacore binding data showing that all constructs containing the 4TSR array bound to fibrillin-2-Ct.

claim: In reciprocal Biacore analysis using ADAMTS6-Ct as the immobilized ligand, its binding to both the N- and C-terminal halves of fibrillin-2 was observed.
source: In reciprocal Biacore analysis using ADAMTS6-Ct as the immobilized ligand, its binding to both the N- and C-terminal halves of fibrillin-2 was observed (Figure 6D, Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by Biacore surface plasmon resonance data shown in Figure 6D and Table 2.

claim: Comparable KD values of 43 nM for fibrillin-2-Nt and 80 nM for fibrillin-2-Ct suggested two or more binding sites in each half of fibrillin-2 with similar affinities for ADAMTS6.
source: Comparable KD values of 43 nM for fibrillin-2-Nt and 80 nM for fibrillin-2-Ct suggested two or more binding sites in each half of fibrillin-2 with similar affinities for ADAMTS6.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Biacore binding data showing similar KD values for ADAMTS6-Ct binding to both halves of fibrillin-2.

claim: The ADAMTS6 binding site on fibrillin-2 may lie in the overlapping region of the two fragments between cbEGF22 and cbEGF24.
source: Alternatively, the ADAMTS6 binding site on fibrillin-2 may lie in the overlapping region of the two fragments between cbEGF22 and cbEGF24.
evidence: This is an alternative interpretation of the Biacore binding data.

claim: ADAMTS6-Ct bound to fibrillin-1 N- and C-terminal halves.
source: Consistent with prior work showing ADAMTS6 binding to fibrillin-1 (Cain et al., 2016), ADAMTS6-Ct bound to fibrillin-1 N- and C-terminal halves (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B)
evidence: The claim is supported by Biacore surface plasmon resonance data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B, and cites a prior publication (Cain et al., 2016) for ADAMTS6 binding to fibrillin-1.

claim: Stronger binding of ADAMTS6-Ct was observed to the N-terminal half of fibrillin-1.
source: although stronger binding was observed to the N-terminal half (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Biacore surface plasmon resonance data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: High-affinity binary interactions suggested that ADAMTS6 binds directly to both fibrillin-1 and fibrillin-2 to cleave them.
source: In summary, these high-affinity binary interactions suggested that ADAMTS6 binds directly to both fibrillin-1 and fibrillin-2 to cleave them.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Biacore binding data showing high-affinity interactions between ADAMTS6 and both fibrillins.

claim: TAILS revealed a putative cleavage site at the Gly2158-His2159 peptide bond in a linker between TGFβ binding-like domain 6 and calcium-binding epidermal growth factor (cbEGF) repeat 32 in the C-terminal half of fibrillin-2.
source: This analysis revealed a putative cleavage site at the Gly2158-His2159 peptide bond in a linker between TGFβ binding-like domain 6 and calcium-binding epidermal growth factor (cbEGF) repeat 32 in the C-terminal half of fibrillin-2 (Figure 7B–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by TAILS N-terminomics data shown in Figure 7B–F.

claim: The sequence of the indicator peptide was semi-tryptic, and therefore unlikely to result from trypsin digestion during sample preparation.
source: The sequence of the indicator peptide, which was semi-tryptic, and therefore unlikely to result from trypsin digestion during sample preparation and the presence of an N-terminal label was determined with high confidence by the MS2 spectrum (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Quantification of the relative ion abundance of isotoptically labeled peptides showed a considerable excess of the Gly2158-His2159 peptide in the presence of active ADAMTS6.
source: Quantification of the relative ion abundance of isotoptically labeled peptides showed a considerable excess of this peptide in the presence of active ADAMTS6 (Figure 7D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by TAILS N-terminomics data shown in Figure 7D–E.

claim: Western blot of the medium showed that ADAMTS6 cleaved the C-terminal half of fibrillin-2.
source: Western blot of the medium from these experiments for orthogonal validation of the cleavage showed that ADAMTS6 cleaved the C-terminal half of fibrillin-2 (Figure 7G).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: The cleavage products of 100 kDa and 75 kDa matched the predicted cleavage fragments in size and their sum matched the expected mass of the FBN2-Ct construct (175 kDa).
source: The cleavage products of 100 kDa and 75 kDa matched the predicted cleavage fragments in size and their sum matched the expected mass of the FBN2-Ct construct (175 kDa).
evidence: This is an observation based on the western blot data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: The Gly2158-His2159 cleavage site is located between two folded, disulfide-bonded domains, predicting separation of the resulting fragments.
source: Importantly, the Gly2158-His2159 cleavage site is located between two folded, disulfide-bonded domains, predicting separation of the resulting fragments (as opposed to cleavage sites within disulfide-bonded fibrillin-2 domains that would remain linked).
evidence: This is an inference based on the location of the cleavage site and knowledge of fibrillin-2 domain structure.

claim: The cleavage can potentially interfere with microfibril assembly, which is reliant on multimerization via C-terminal interactions downstream of the cleavage site.
source: The cleavage can potentially interfere with microfibril assembly, which is reliant on multimerization via C-terminal interactions downstream of the cleavage site (Hubmacher et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference based on the location of the cleavage site and knowledge of microfibril assembly mechanisms, citing a prior publication (Hubmacher et al., 2008).

claim: TAILS revealed a putative cleavage site at the R516-A517 peptide bond in a linker between EGF4 and cbEGF3 in the N-terminal half of fibrillin-1.
source: A targeted search for fibrillin-1 peptides with labeled N-termini revealed a putative cleavage site at the R516-A517 peptide bond in a linker between EGF4 and cbEGF3 in the N-terminal half (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by TAILS N-terminomics data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The peptide sequence and presence of an N-terminal label for the R516-A517 fibrillin-1 cleavage site was determined with high confidence by the MS2 spectrum.
source: The peptide sequence and presence of an N-terminal label was determined with high confidence by the MS2 spectrum and quantification of the ion abundance showed a considerable excess of this peptide in the presence of ADAMTS6 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C-E).
evidence: The claim is supported by TAILS N-terminomics data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C-E.

claim: Quantification of the ion abundance showed a considerable excess of the R516-A517 fibrillin-1 peptide in the presence of ADAMTS6.
source: The peptide sequence and presence of an N-terminal label was determined with high confidence by the MS2 spectrum and quantification of the ion abundance showed a considerable excess of this peptide in the presence of ADAMTS6 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C-E).
evidence: The claim is supported by TAILS N-terminomics data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C-E.

claim: TAILS revealed several potential cleavage sites in fibronectin by ADAMTS6.
source: By comparing the ratio of light:heavy dimethyl-labeled peptides, TAILS revealed several potential cleavage sites in the medium from the ADAMTS6 sample (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A) (Table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by TAILS N-terminomics data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and Table 3.

claim: Fbn2 haploinsufficiency dramatically restored the external craniofacial and hindlimb morphology of Adamts6 mutants.
source: Fbn2 haploinsufficiency dramatically restored the external craniofacial and hindlimb morphology of Adamts6 mutants as well as the maturity, length and shape of skeletal components of the hindlimb and axial skeleton (Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, B, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological and skeletal analysis data shown in Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, B, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Fbn2 haploinsufficiency restored the maturity, length and shape of skeletal components of the hindlimb and axial skeleton in Adamts6 mutants.
source: Fbn2 haploinsufficiency dramatically restored the external craniofacial and hindlimb morphology of Adamts6 mutants as well as the maturity, length and shape of skeletal components of the hindlimb and axial skeleton (Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, B, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological and skeletal analysis data shown in Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, B, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated reversal of reduced crown-rump length in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos.
source: Specifically, alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated reversal of reduced crown-rump length, long bone shortening and improved ossification of hindlimb long bones and ribs, an appropriately segmented sternum with a normal xiphoid process and normal fontanelle closure (Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated reversal of long bone shortening in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos.
source: Specifically, alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated reversal of reduced crown-rump length, long bone shortening and improved ossification of hindlimb long bones and ribs, an appropriately segmented sternum with a normal xiphoid process and normal fontanelle closure (Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated improved ossification of hindlimb long bones and ribs in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos.
source: Specifically, alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated reversal of reduced crown-rump length, long bone shortening and improved ossification of hindlimb long bones and ribs, an appropriately segmented sternum with a normal xiphoid process and normal fontanelle closure (Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos had an appropriately segmented sternum with a normal xiphoid process.
source: Specifically, alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated reversal of reduced crown-rump length, long bone shortening and improved ossification of hindlimb long bones and ribs, an appropriately segmented sternum with a normal xiphoid process and normal fontanelle closure (Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos had normal fontanelle closure.
source: Specifically, alizarin red and alcian blue-stained skeletal preparations demonstrated reversal of reduced crown-rump length, long bone shortening and improved ossification of hindlimb long bones and ribs, an appropriately segmented sternum with a normal xiphoid process and normal fontanelle closure (Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Cleft secondary palate which occurred with a high incidence in Adamts6-/- embryos, was not observed in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos.
source: In addition, cleft secondary palate which occurred with a high incidence in Adamts6-/- embryos, was not observed in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimb fibrillin-2 staining showed reduced intensity comparable to wild type hindlimb.
source: Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimb fibrillin-2 staining showed reduced intensity comparable to wild type hindlimb (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: Aggrecan, cartilage link protein and Sox9 staining intensity in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- femur growth plates were restored to comparable levels as in wild type limbs.
source: Aggrecan, cartilage link protein and Sox9 staining intensity in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- femur growth plates were restored to comparable levels as in wild type limbs, indicating restoration of the appropriate ECM of cartilage (Figure 8D, Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8D and Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: Fbn2+/- embryos had normal hindlimb development and growth plate zone organization as wild type controls.
source: Fbn2+/- embryos had normal hindlimb development and growth plate zone organization as wild type controls (Figure 8—figure supplement 3, Figure 8—figure supplement 4C-E).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological and histological data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3 and Figure 8—figure supplement 4C-E.

claim: Adamts6-/- embryos with ~80% reduction in fibrillin-1 levels (Adamts6-/-;Fbn1mgR/mgR embryos) had no amelioration of limb defects.
source: In contrast to Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- embryos, Adamts6-/- embryos with ~80% reduction in fibrillin-1 levels (Adamts6-/-;Fbn1mgR/mgR embryos) had no amelioration of limb defects (Figure 8—figure supplement 5A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological and skeletal analysis data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 5A, B.

claim: Genetic analyses using well-characterized Fbn1 and Fbn2 mutants suggested a specific role for ADAMTS6 in modulating fibrillin-2 abundance during limb microfibril proteostasis.
source: Taken together, these genetic analyses using well-characterized Fbn1 and Fbn2 mutants, suggested a specific role for ADAMTS6 in modulating fibrillin-2 abundance during limb microfibril proteostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the genetic rescue experiments showing that Fbn2 haploinsufficiency, but not Fbn1 reduction, rescues Adamts6-/- phenotypes.

claim: Adamts6-/- hindlimb long bones had reduced pSmad1/5/8 staining compared to wild type.
source: Adamts6-/- hindlimb long bones had reduced pSmad1/5/8 staining compared to wild type, which was restored to wild type levels in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimbs (Figure 9A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9A, B.

claim: pSmad1/5/8 staining was restored to wild type levels in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimbs.
source: Adamts6-/- hindlimb long bones had reduced pSmad1/5/8 staining compared to wild type, which was restored to wild type levels in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimbs (Figure 9A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9A, B.

claim: pSMAD5 was reduced in Adamts6-/- hindlimb extracts.
source: Similarily, pSMAD5 was reduced in Adamts6-/- hindlimb extracts and restored to normal levels in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimb extracts (Figure 9C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 9C, D.

claim: pSMAD5 was restored to normal levels in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimb extracts.
source: Similarily, pSMAD5 was reduced in Adamts6-/- hindlimb extracts and restored to normal levels in Adamts6-/-;Fbn2+/- hindlimb extracts (Figure 9C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 9C, D.

claim: No change in TGFβ signaling, as measured by pSMAD2 immunostaining and western blot, occurred in Adamts6-/- hindlimbs.
source: In contrast, no change in TGFβ signaling, as measured by pSMAD2 immunostaining and western blot, occurred in Adamts6-/- hindlimbs (Figure 9E–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence and western blot data shown in Figure 9E–H.

claim: Stronger co-localized fibrillin-2 and GDF5 signal was consistently observed in Adamts6 mutant knee joint mesenchyme.
source: We consistently observed stronger co-localized fibrillin-2 and GDF5 signal in Adamts6 mutant knee joint mesenchyme, as well as in the perichondrium and interjoint regions in distal limbs, which are at less mature stages of development and have abundant undifferentiated limb mesenchyme (illustrated in knee joint interzone in Figure 10A–C, Figure 10—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 10A–C and Figure 10—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Stronger co-localized fibrillin-2 and GDF5 signal was observed in the perichondrium and interjoint regions in distal limbs of Adamts6 mutants.
source: We consistently observed stronger co-localized fibrillin-2 and GDF5 signal in Adamts6 mutant knee joint mesenchyme, as well as in the perichondrium and interjoint regions in distal limbs, which are at less mature stages of development and have abundant undifferentiated limb mesenchyme (illustrated in knee joint interzone in Figure 10A–C, Figure 10—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 10A–C and Figure 10—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Increased fibrillin-2 was associated with increased GDF5 sequestration in Adamts6-deficent limbs.
source: Thus, increased fibrillin-2 was associated with increased GDF5 sequestration in Adamts6-deficent limbs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the immunofluorescence data showing co-localization of fibrillin-2 and GDF5 in Adamts6 mutant limbs.
